concept.title: Complex Firefox policy families
concept.shortdesc: Review nested policy families as groups because one exported value can combine several related browser behaviors.

section.title: Extensions
section.p: Use Step 6, Extensions, for allowed, blocked, required-install, locked, and update rules represented by ExtensionSettings; use legacy Extensions only when that shape matches the intended Firefox behavior. AMO search is a user-initiated, optional name lookup. BPM does not fetch an XPI or use an AMO result URL for installation. When AMO is unavailable, enter the manual GUID and validated install-URL.

section.title: Permissions
section.p: Permissions groups camera, microphone, location, notification, autoplay, and similar decisions. Review allow/block lists together because a domain can be affected by more than one permission branch.

section.title: Updates
section.p: Update controls such as DisableAppUpdate, AppAutoUpdate, and DisableSystemAddonUpdate should be reviewed as one family so users understand which updater remains active.

section.title: Certificates and trust
section.p: Use Step 4, Certificates & trust, for Certificates, enterprise-root choices, authentication, and SecurityDevices. Certificate and device paths are literal references. BPM does not upload, open, hash, read, or validate certificate or device contents; verify trust behavior outside BPM before deployment.

section.title: Proxy
section.p: Proxy combines mode, server, port, and protocol reuse. Validate manual proxy values carefully because malformed addresses can block browser network access.

section.title: Search, URLs, sites, and homepage
section.p: Step 1 owns SearchEngines; Step 2 owns Homepage, startup, site filters, handlers, and managed bookmarks. Search URL templates must keep {searchTerms}. Unsafe or unsupported imported URL/site shapes are preserved for review rather than silently normalized.

section.title: Privacy and AI controls
section.p: Privacy families such as EnableTrackingProtection and Cookies can interact with site exceptions. Firefox AI controls such as AIControls are product policies to document; they do not add AI functionality to the documentation portal. With the Release 153 or ESR 153.0 schema selected, use Step 7, AI, to configure Smart Window with AIControls.SmartWindow: choose available or blocked for Value and set Locked when users must not change it.
